newsitem.title: BELGIUM: MEPs to vote on 284 amendments to BSE report on Feb 5.
newsitem.headline: MEPs to vote on 284 amendments to BSE report on Feb 5.

text.p: Euro MP's are due to start voting on February 5 on 284 amendments to a draft report on the mad cow crisis prepared by Spanish MEP Manuel Medina Ortega, parliamentary sources said on Wednesday.
The report, which follows a four month investigation by a special committee of inquiry, criticised the European Commission and Britain for mishandling the crisis since it broke in March 1996.
"Members of the inquiry have hardened their position," said a parliamentary official, adding that voting could continue for two days due to the large number of amendments.

For instance, the president of the inquiry, German Christian Democrat Reimer Boege, now supports a vote of censure if the Commission has not improved its veterinary services and controls, the official noted.
A Commission spokesman said on Wednesday that the Commission will shortly announce changes to achieve this.
The appointment of Consumer Policy Commissioner Emma Bonino to take responsibility for a new food safety agency will be confirmed shortly, the spokesman added.
Parliamentary legal experts said that the vote of censure against the Commission must be requested by at least 63 MEPs, or 10 percent of all members.
A majority of 314 votes and two-thirds of votes cast are needed for the vote of censure to be successful.
A case brought before the European Court of Justice against Britain for failing to take all necessary action to eradicate and control BSE would have to respect strict time constraints.
The case, as well as another seeking damages from Britain, where most BSE cases have been reported, would have to be initiated by the European Commission on behalf of the parliament.
Families of victims of Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease, the human equivalent of BSE, or farmers who have suffered loss of revenue could also make claims, officials said.
The European Parliament is due to vote on the BSE inquiry committee's report on February 19.
